summary: API Gateway queue resonance causing upstream GPU driver reset and elevated 5xx rate
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12T15:20Z we observed a rapid increase in 5xx responses for a small subset of requests from a ClearHorizon Labs tenant on dedicated capacity. Impact: ~8% 5xx rate for that tenant over a 30m window, intermittent user-facing failures for chat and embedding endpoints. Environment: prod | us-west-2 | dedicated pool serving mixed chat+embeddings workload. Steps to reproduce: 1) Replay customer traffic profile (mixed small chat + large embedding batches) against serving pool. 2) Ramp concurrent short streaming sessions while running large embedding batches. 3) Observe apigw accept queue growth, prolonged queue head waits, and eventual upstream runtime signals. Observed behavior: API Gateway accept/worker queue length oscillates (resonance) under mixed traffic, producing bursts of long queue head latency. During these bursts an upstream runtime process on a subset of nodes trips the GPU driver (NVML) reset, causing the runtime to restart and propagate 502/503 responses. Timeline: 15:18Z - first minor spike in queue length; 15:22Z - repeated oscillation pattern begins; 15:27Z - first upstream GPU reset observed in driver logs; 15:30Z - customer reports user-facing failures. Initial mitigation: rate-limited incoming connections for affected tenant, temporarily diverted heavy embedding jobs to a cooler pool, and scaled up ephemeral proxy count to reduce per-proxy queue depth.
investigation_notes: Checked apigw metrics: accept_queue_length exhibited periodic amplifications with ~6-12s period aligned with customer burst windows.
Runtime logs show NVML driver reset on worker nodes node-uw2-5 and node-uw2-9 at 2026-03-12T15:27:41Z and 15:29:03Z respectively.
dmesg on affected nodes contains gpu-reset backtraces; no OOMs were reported by kernel prior to reset.
Trace sampling from ingress -> proxy -> runtime shows multiple in-flight requests piling behind long-polling embedding batches; head-of-queue latency spikes correlate with driver resets.

Hypothesis: Accept queue resonance amplifies small clock jitter in proxy worker wakeups, causing clustered dispatch to a few runtimes which transiently overcommit GPU scheduling and trigger driver watchdog resets.
We reproduced a similar but lower-amplitude pattern in staging by replaying the customer's mixed workload and toggling proxy worker counts.
Checked for recent deploys: No serving-runtime binary changes in the 48h window; a config sweep to proxy keepalive was rolled out 36h prior (linked PR), possible interaction.
Collected nvml and runtime core dumps (attached to internal S3) and perf traces for follow-up by GPU team.
mitigation: Applied temporary tenant-level rate cap to smooth accept queue ingress.
Re-routed heavy embedding jobs to a dedicated 'batch-cooler' pool to avoid coupling with interactive chat traffic.
Increased ephemeral proxy replica count for us-west-2 affected AZs to reduce per-proxy queue depth and observed immediate reduction in queue resonance amplitude.
Added short-term autoscaler hint to pre-warm additional runtimes when mixed workload signals are detected.
